lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: There was a table set out under a tree in front of the house, and the March Hare and the Hatter were having tea at it: a Dormouse was sitting between them, fast asleep, and the other two were using it as a cushion, resting their elbows on it, and talking over its head.

lines.speaker: Alice

lines.speaker: Alice

lines.speaker: Hatter
lines.text: “I’m getting tired of this. I vote the young lady tells us a story.”

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: said Alice, rather alarmed at the proposal.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: And they pinched it on both sides at once.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The Dormouse slowly opened his eyes.

The Hatter was the only one who got any advantage from the change: and Alice was a good deal worse off than before, as the March Hare had just upset the milk-jug into his plate.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Alice did not wish to offend the Dormouse again, so she began very cautiously:

lines.speaker: Alice
lines.text: “But I don’t understand. Where did they draw the treacle from?”

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: This answer so confused poor Alice, that she let the Dormouse go on for some time without interrupting it.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: the Dormouse went on, yawning and rubbing its eyes, for it was getting very sleepy;

lines.text: The Dormouse had closed its eyes by this time, and was going off into a doze; but, on being pinched by the Hatter, it woke up again with a little shriek, and went on:

lines.speaker: Dormouse
lines.text: “—that begins with an M, such as mouse-traps, and the moon, and memory, and muchness—you know you say things are “much of a muchness”

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: This piece of rudeness was more than Alice could bear: she got up in great disgust, and walked off; the Dormouse fell asleep instantly, and neither of the others took the least notice of her going, though she looked back once or twice, half hoping that they would call after her: the last time she saw them, they were trying to put the Dormouse into the teapot.

lines.speaker: Alice
lines.text: “At any rate I’ll never go there again!”

lines.speaker: Narrator

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: “But everything’s curious today. I think I may as well go in at once.”

lines.speaker: Narrator

Then she went to work nibbling at the mushroom (she had kept a piece of it in her pocket) till she was about a foot high: then she walked down the little passage: and then—she found herself at last in the beautiful garden, among the bright flower-beds and the cool fountains.
